items.text: Seedance 2.5 1080p on @TapNow_AI Prompt: 7-shot handheld phone vlog montage, photorealistic snapshot realism, varied angles/cuts, slight tilt/shake, harsh fluorescent gym light mixed with warm high-window afternoon sun, fine film grain. Woman Image1: use reference only for face/hairstyle; fitted heather-grey short-sleeve athletic top, black leggings, tied-back hair with loose strands. Alone in a quiet scuffed gym corner with folded mats, spotted mirror, bench with rolled yoga mat/water bottle. Natural Korean dialogue/reactions, live ambient SFX only, no music/text/logos/watermarks. 1 (0-2s): Rope catches her foot; she stumbles and laughs. Close, low, drifting camera. “아 뭐야 벌써”. 2 (2-4s): Side close-up of hands/rope resetting; wrist flicks, rope slaps floor twice, then finds rhythm. Shaky follow. 3 (4-6s): Straight-on steady jump-rope rhythm, focused half-smile, quicker breathing, rope blur. “하나, 둘, 셋…” 4 (6-8s): Rope hits shin; she winces/laughs, hops once, restarts. Slight upward angle, slow push-in. “Okay, still counts.” 5 (8-10s): Faster set, sweat at hairline, heavy breathing, rapid rope beats. Straight-on, gentle sway, motion blur. 6 (10-13s): Rope tangles; she stops, doubles over laughing, hands on knees, shoulders shaking. Camera tilts down. “아 못하겠다 진짜”. 7 (13-15s): Still laughing/breathless, slowly straightens, wipes eyes, drops rope, grinning. Camera drifts back/up and lingers. Only her throughout; authentic fumbling, laughter, breathing, footsteps, rope impacts/drop, faint distant gym ambience. Do not depict/copy the reference image itself.

items.text: Midjourney Image and Prompt: 30s cinematic Indian flower-market physical comedy, 9 shots, playful opening → accidental garland snag → sudden panic → escalating chase → progressively accumulating flowers → increasingly ridiculous appearance → exhausted stop → “Flower King” reveal → warm comedic payoff. Fast-paced but highly readable, strong physical cause-and-effect, continuous forward progression through one connected market lane, natural canine body mechanics, varied reactions and obstacles, no repetitive running beats, minimal slow motion. REFERENCE INPUTS: Use @GOLDEN_RETRIEVER_REFERENCE for the SAME Golden Retriever throughout. Use @FLOWER_VENDOR_REFERENCE for the SAME Indian flower vendor throughout. Use @MARIGOLD_GARLAND_REFERENCE for the orange-and-yellow marigold garlands throughout. Use @INDIAN_FLOWER_MARKET_REFERENCE for the SAME continuous Indian flower market throughout. STRICT REFERENCE LOCK: Exactly ONE main Golden Retriever based on @GOLDEN_RETRIEVER_REFERENCE. Preserve its exact warm golden fur, fluffy chest, floppy ears, dark brown eyes, black nose, body proportions and fluffy tail. The Golden Retriever wears NO collar, clothes or accessories at the beginning. Exactly ONE main flower vendor based on @FLOWER_VENDOR_REFERENCE. Preserve his exact face, black mustache, beige shirt, white trousers, brown sandals and orange scarf. All major flower garlands follow @MARIGOLD_GARLAND_REFERENCE: dense orange and golden-yellow marigold flowers, flexible connected strands with occasional green leaves. No artificial plastic garlands. No dog clones. No duplicate main vendor. No costume changes. No disappearing flowers. Background vendors and shoppers remain secondary characters only. ENVIRONMENT LOCK: The entire sequence takes place inside ONE continuous flower market based on @INDIAN_FLOWER_MARKET_REFERENCE. Preserve the same narrow central pedestrian lane, flower stalls on both sides, wooden stall frames, hanging marigold garlands, baskets of flowers, scattered petals, fabric awnings, colorful weathered buildings and warm morning sunlight. The Golden Retriever begins beside the main vendor's stall and continuously travels deeper along the SAME central market path. The main flower vendor follows behind the dog on foot. The market does NOT transform into unrelated streets or locations. The dog never teleports. GLOBAL CONTINUITY LOCK: At 0:00 the Golden Retriever has NO flowers attached to its body. The first circular marigold garland becomes caught loosely around the dog's neck at approximately 0:04. Once attached, this first garland NEVER disappears. At approximately 0:07, the first garland pulls a connected long flower strand from the stall. That strand remains physically connected and trails behind the running dog until it tears free from the stall. Every later flower contact adds MORE flowers to the dog's body. Flower accumulation must be progressive: no flowers → one neck garland → one trailing strand → several loose strands → flowers around shoulders and torso → additional garlands across back → final heavily decorated “Flower King.” Flowers NEVER reset between shots. Do not suddenly cover the dog completely in one cut. The transformation must happen gradually through visible physical contacts. The dog's face, eyes and nose remain visible throughout. Flowers may wrap loosely around neck, shoulders, torso and back but NEVER dangerously tighten around the dog's throat or legs. The dog remains able to run naturally on all four paws. Any flowers pulled from a stall remain missing from that stall afterward. Fallen petals remain on the ground. SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:03 | SOMETHING SMELLS GOOD The Golden Retriever from @GOLDEN_RETRIEVER_REFERENCE wanders curiously beside the main flower stall inside @INDIAN_FLOWER_MARKET_REFERENCE. The flower vendor from @FLOWER_VENDOR_REFERENCE is arranging bright orange and yellow marigold garlands. The dog notices a large circular marigold garland hanging low from the edge of the stall. Its ears perk slightly. It steps closer. Its nose moves toward the flowers. The Golden sniffs enthusiastically, tail wagging. The vendor remains focused on arranging another basket. SHOT 2 — 0:03–0:06 | UH-OH The Golden pushes its nose slightly deeper through the center of the hanging circular garland. The garland slips over its muzzle. The dog instinctively raises its head. The flexible flower loop slides backward over its ears and settles loosely around its neck. The Golden freezes. Its tail stops. It looks downward at the orange flowers around its chest. One beat. The dog suddenly shakes its head rapidly trying to remove them. The garland stays attached. The Golden's eyes widen. SHOT 3 — 0:06–0:09 | PANIC The frightened Golden jumps backward. The neck garland catches ONE long connected marigold strand hanging from the stall. The dog bolts forward. The long flower strand stretches tight behind it. Several hanging garlands jerk sideways. The flower vendor feels the sudden pull. He turns. His expression changes from confusion to alarm. He reaches toward the flowers— too late. The long strand pulls free from the stall. The Golden races down the central market lane with orange flowers streaming behind it. The vendor immediately runs after the dog. SHOT 4 — 0:09–0:12 | FLOWER TRAIL The Golden runs between the crowded flower stalls. The long marigold strand bounces and snakes across the ground behind it. The trailing strand brushes against a low basket overflowing with loose marigold blossoms. The basket tilts. A wave of lightweight orange and yellow flowers spills onto the path. The Golden hears the noise behind it. It briefly looks backward while still running. Seeing the bouncing flower strand “chasing” it makes the dog panic even more. It accelerates. The vendor carefully hops around the spilled flowers and keeps chasing. SHOT 5 — 0:12–0:15 | MORE FLOWERS The Golden passes beneath several low hanging garlands stretched between two stall posts. One loose garland brushes across the dog's shoulders. Another catches gently across its upper back. The dog lowers its head and pushes forward. The flexible garlands slide free from their hooks and travel with the dog. Now the Golden has: one garland around its neck, one long trailing strand, and two additional loose flower strands draped across its shoulders and back. The dog emerges from beneath them looking increasingly decorated. It keeps running. SHOT 6 — 0:15–0:19 | THE MARKET REACTS The Golden enters a busier section of the flower market. People notice the bizarre flower-covered dog approaching. One shopper holding a flower basket quickly steps sideways. The Golden curves around her rather than colliding. Its trailing garland swings outward from the turn. The swinging flowers lightly brush another display of hanging marigold loops. Two more lightweight loops fall naturally across the Golden's torso and back. Orange petals explode softly into the air. The dog shakes its torso once while running. Instead of removing the flowers, the shake redistributes them around its fluffy coat. The Golden now looks even more ridiculous. Background vendors begin laughing and pointing. The main flower vendor continues chasing behind, increasingly exhausted. SHOT 7 — 0:19–0:23 | MAXIMUM FLOWER CHAOS The Golden sees another curtain of hanging marigold garlands ahead. It tries a new strategy. Instead of running straight through, the dog lowers its chest and quickly ducks beneath the lowest opening. Its body clears most of the garlands— but its fluffy raised tail catches ONE final loose strand. The strand slips free from the stall. As the Golden continues forward, it slides along the dog's back and settles loosely around its waist and shoulders. The Golden emerges from the flowers. It is now covered in many layers of orange and yellow marigold garlands while its face remains completely visible. The long trailing strand finally catches lightly on a low empty wooden post. The tension pulls it free from the dog's existing garlands. The trailing section drops harmlessly onto the ground. The flowers already wrapped around the Golden remain attached. SHOT 8 — 0:23–0:27 | THE FLOWER KING The Golden finally reaches a small open area at the end of the connected market lane. It slows from sprint → trot → walk. Then stops. The exhausted dog pants heavily. It looks down at itself. Orange and yellow marigold garlands cover its neck, chest, shoulders, torso and back like an absurd ceremonial costume. Several loose flowers sit naturally on top of its head. Its golden face remains perfectly visible between the flowers. The Golden slowly raises its head. Its posture becomes unexpectedly proud. Its tail begins wagging again. Nearby shoppers stop. Everyone stares. The dog now looks like a majestic accidental “Flower King.” SHOT 9 — 0:27–0:30 | LONG LIVE THE KING The exhausted flower vendor finally reaches the open area. He bends forward with both hands on his knees, breathing heavily. He looks up at the Golden. He freezes. The Golden sits upright in the center of the market, completely decorated in orange-and-yellow marigold garlands. Its chest is raised proudly. Its tail sweeps happily across the ground. The vendor's frustrated expression slowly disappears. He begins laughing. Nearby vendors and shoppers laugh and clap. The Golden looks around at everyone. It misunderstands the attention as praise. It lifts its chin even higher and gives ONE happy bark. A loose marigold flower slowly slips from the top of its head and lands directly in front of its paws. The Golden looks down at it. Then proudly looks forward again. CUT TO BLACK. MOTION LOCK: Golden Retriever: curious walk → sniff → accidental head-through-garland → freeze → head shake → backward jump → panic sprint → backward glance → accelerate → duck → curved avoidance → running body shake → low duck → gradual slowdown → proud sit. Flower progression: stall display → first neck garland → connected trailing strand → shoulder garlands → back garlands → torso garlands → final heavily decorated Flower King. Vendor: arrange flowers → notice pull → reach → chase → hop around spilled flowers → continue chase → increasingly exhausted → arrive → frustration → realization → laugh. Every chase beat must introduce a DIFFERENT physical interaction. Do NOT show repetitive straight running for the entire sequence. FLOWER ACCUMULATION LOCK: 0:00–0:03 = ZERO flowers on dog. 0:03–0:06 = ONE neck garland. 0:06–0:12 = neck garland + ONE long trailing strand. 0:12–0:15 = add shoulder/back strands. 0:15–0:19 = add several torso/back loops. 0:19–0:23 = add final garland layers while trailing strand detaches. 0:23–0:30 = final Flower King appearance remains unchanged. Flowers only accumulate after visible contact. No magical appearance of flowers. No reset to clean fur after flowers have attached. The dog's face must remain unobstructed and recognizable at all times. CAMERA: Begin close enough to clearly show the Golden sniffing the low circular garland and accidentally pushing its head through it. Keep the first garland snag visually readable in one continuous action. Use side tracking when the Golden first bolts away so the stretched long marigold strand and chasing vendor are visible together. Use wider views through the market to establish the continuous path and flower stalls ahead. For each new garland interaction, frame the dog's full body clearly enough to show WHERE the flowers make contact and HOW they become attached. Use low forward tracking briefly when the Golden looks backward and sees the flowers trailing behind. Use side tracking for the curved avoidance and body shake. At 0:19, show the low duck beneath the hanging flower curtain from a readable side angle. At 0:23, transition from frantic tracking into a stable wider composition as the Golden slows down. For the Flower King reveal, briefly hold a centered full-body view of the decorated Golden sitting proudly among the colorful market. Finish with BOTH the exhausted vendor and decorated Golden visible, surrounded by amused market shoppers. AUDIO: Warm lively Indian flower-market ambience throughout: vendors talking, distant pedestrians, baskets moving, light street activity and occasional bicycle bells. Use playful upbeat Indian instrumental music: light tabla rhythm, playful sitar melody and small dhol accents. 0:00–0:03: gentle sitar and relaxed market ambience. 0:04: soft flower rustle as the garland slides over the dog's head. 0:05: music briefly pauses when the Golden freezes. 0:06: quick playful tabla accent as the dog suddenly bolts. 0:06–0:12: tabla rhythm accelerates with running paws. Continuous soft rustling from the trailing marigold strand. 0:09: basket tipping sound followed by soft flowers scattering across the ground. 0:12–0:19: add energetic dhol accents as more garlands accumulate. Synchronize each new flower snag with a light comedic percussion hit. 0:19–0:23: music reaches its fastest playful rhythm during the final flower chaos. 0:23: percussion gradually slows as the Golden slows down. 0:25: brief musical pause for the Flower King reveal. 0:27: one warm comedic sitar flourish as the vendor sees the decorated dog. Market laughter and gentle applause rise. 0:29: ONE cheerful Golden Retriever bark. Finish with a short playful tabla + sitar flourish. No dialogue. No narration.
